catalog_quote: ¶ CAP. XX. DE EL ACCENTO. LOS nombres bisilabos tienen el accento en la primera silaba Pecne madre. Puxcu hermana. Guozuc hozico, y los mas son bisilabos, o monosilabos, quando son trisilabos en la penultima. ¶ Los Aduerbios y partes indeclinables comunmente tienen el accento en la vltima, Yele presto, Texat a baxo, Tactu arriba. Yequem de que manera Henta, epta, &c. ¶ Los verbos en las primeras de Singular de el Indicatiuo, y en las segundas de Singular y Plural hazen accento en la penultima, y en las de mas en la antepenultima ¶ El Imperatiuo todo tiene el acento en la vltima y el presente de infinitiuo y gerundio de Accusatiuo. ¶ Los demas tiempos en la penultima comunmente. Algunas excepciones ay destas quatro reglas, que con el vso se sabran. AD MAIOREM DEI GLORIAM.

new_statements.quote: LOS nombres bisílabos tienen el accento en la primera sílaba Pecne madre. Puxcu hermana. Guozuc hozico, y los mas son bisílabos, o monosílabos, quando son trisílabos en la penúltima. ¶ Los Aduerbios y partes indeclinables comúnmente tienen el accento en la vltima, Yele presto, Texat a baxo, Tactu arriba [...] ¶ Los verbos en las primeras de Singular de el Indicatiuo, y en las segundas de Singular y Plural hazen accento en la penúltima, y en las de mas en la antepenúltima ¶ El Imperatiuo todo tiene el acento en la vltima y el presente de infinitiuo y gerundio de Accusatiuo. ¶ Los demas tiempos en la penúltima comunmente. Algunas excepciones ay destas quatro reglas, que con el vso se sabrán.
new_statements.translation: Disyllabic nouns have the accent on the first syllable: Pecne 'mother', Puxcu 'sister', Guozuc 'snout'; and most [nouns] are disyllables or monosyllables; when they are trisyllables, [the accent is] on the penult. Adverbs and indeclinable parts of speech commonly have the accent on the last syllable: Yele 'quickly', Texat 'below', Tactu 'above' [...]. Verbs in the first person singular of the indicative and in the second persons singular and plural have the accent on the penult, and in the other [persons] on the antepenult. The whole imperative has the accent on the last syllable, as do the present infinitive and the accusative gerund. The other tenses commonly on the penult. There are some exceptions to these four rules, which will be learned by usage.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word-class-conditioned system described in four rules. Nouns: penultimate (a disyllable's first syllable is its penult; trisyllables explicitly penult; most nouns are mono- or disyllabic). Adverbs and other indeclinables: usually final. Verbs: penult in 1sg indicative and 2sg/2pl, antepenult in the other persons; final in the imperative, present infinitive and 'accusative gerund'; penult in the remaining tenses. Coded fixed: penultimate syllable because the nominal (lexical-word) rule is penult and the default for other tenses is penult; an alternative coding would be a morphologically conditioned (category/inflection-sensitive) system, and 'fixed: initial syllable' if one takes the disyllabic-noun formulation literally.
new_statements.exceptions: Adverbs and indeclinables take final accent (explicitly contrasted with disyllabic nouns); verbal persons/moods redistribute the accent between penult, antepenult and final; 'Algunas excepciones ay destas quatro reglas, que con el vso se sabrán' (some exceptions to these four rules exist, to be learned by use).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent of citation forms as heard by a Jesuit missionary c. 1600 ('accento' in the Latin-grammar sense); no phonetic detail, no phrase-level information. Márquez Miranda 1943 restates the same rules second-hand in his vocabulary notes (e.g. PDF pp. 19, 26, 64, 72, 99). The parallel Allentiac Arte (alle1239) was not checked.
new_statements.identity_note: The source is Valdivia's 1607 Arte for Millcayac, the Huarpe language of Mendoza (mill1237), as distinct from the sister language Allentiac of San Juan (alle1239), for which Valdivia printed a parallel Arte (reprinted Medina 1894, Mitre 1894). The Millcayac Arte survives in the copy Márquez Miranda found in the Jesuit library of the Universidad del Cuzco (Peru) and reproduced in facsimile in 1943; Schuller's 1913 Harvard fragment (fol. 12 Doctrina, fol. 21 Confessionario) contains no accent material, and Cancino's 2017 Casanatense find is a copy of the Doctrina/catecismo/confesionario, not the Arte.

sources.locator: Arte Millcayac, Cap. XX 'De el accento', fol. 24 recto = Márquez Miranda 1943: 217 (PDF p. 155, right-hand column)
sources.note: Chapter XX 'De el accento' gives four rules: disyllabic nouns stressed on the first syllable (Pecne 'mother', Puxcu 'sister', Guozuc 'snout'), trisyllabic nouns on the penult; adverbs and indeclinables commonly on the last syllable (Yele, Texat, Tactu, Yequem); verbs 1sg indicative and 2sg/2pl on the penult, other persons antepenult; imperative, present infinitive and accusative gerund on the last syllable; other tenses commonly penult; 'some exceptions to these four rules'.
